title: Azoth unit vocabulary
description: The canonical units a spec may declare, each with the dimension it carries and the name it has in `uom` and in `pint`. This is the one hand-written source for that list; `tools/gen_vocabulary.py` compiles it into Rust, Python and JSON Schema, and `--check` fails if any of the three has drifted. **No magnitude appears in it, with one exception that the display table states.** A scale unit's conversion factor is a number the units libraries already know, and restating one here would be a second answer to a question they have answered - the failure that produced this repository's millimetre defect. `additionalProperties: false` throughout, so a field cannot be added without a deliberate edit here.

schema_version.description: Bump only if the format changes; the generator refuses a version it does not know rather than guessing at what a newer shape meant. Version 2 added `unit_sets` and version 3 `display_units`, neither of which an earlier table carries and neither of which can be read without.

slots.description: The base dimensions, in the order every exponent tuple below is written in. The order is uom::si::ISQ's, and it is not cosmetic: the generated exponent tuples and the generated uom quantity types are both built from it, so a different order permutes all of them at once.

dimensions.description: Every dimension a unit below carries, named once. A unit refers to one by id, so two units that share a dimension cannot be given different exponents by accident.

display_units.description: The units a *display* may switch to and a spec may not declare. **Why they are a separate table and not rows above**: `specs/schema/unit.schema.json` - the enum a spec's `unit:` is checked against - is generated from `units`, so keeping an affine unit out of *this* table is what makes "no spec may name one" a generated fact rather than a rule somebody has to remember. It is also what the Lean map needs: every `units` row makes a dimension claim that `lean/Azoth/Gate.lean` proves, and a unit declared for presentation makes no such claim. **A row here carries numbers**, which a row above deliberately does not: a scale unit's factor is one `uom` and `pint` both know, while an affine unit's offset is the unit's own *definition* - 273.15 K for °C, 459.67 °R for °F - which neither library exposes as data. The check that makes them trustworthy is the same one: `python/tests/test_units_cross_library.py` holds each affine conversion to `pint`'s own answer for the unit, at two values because an affine conversion is pinned by two.

unit_sets.description: The named sets a reader may switch a display between, each naming one unit per dimension. A set is a *choice* and not a conversion: every unit it names is a row above, with its own `pint` name and its own conversion, and the set says only which of them to read. A dimension no set names has no engineering alternative and is read in the unit the library computed it in, so a set may be partial without any display falling back to a blank.

dimension_id.description: A dimension's name, unique within `dimensions`. The generator refuses a duplicate rather than letting the last one win.

exponents.description: One exponent per slot, in the order `slots` declares. The bound is well inside the i8 the generated Rust carries, so a value that would overflow is refused here rather than at codegen.

uom_path.description: Where uom carries this dimension, as `<dimension module>::<unit>` - the path `.new::<..>()` takes. The quantity type is not part of it: the generator derives that from the exponents, so a wrong exponent fails to compile instead of being waved through by a matching name. The module is checked against the dimension's own quantity, because uom's module for a quantity is its name in snake case.

id.description: The canonical unit string, exactly as a spec spells it in `unit:`. This is the string that reaches a user, so it is the one entry in the table that is a readable unit rather than an identifier.

pint.description: The unit's name in pint's registry. pint supplies the conversion factor, which is why none is written down.

uom.description: Where uom carries this dimension. Absent in two cases: where uom has no such quantity at all - uom's `quantity!` macro must run inside `uom::si`, and the `Units` trait that makes `.new::<u>()` compile is assembled by `system!` from a closed list, so no crate outside uom can add a quantity to it - and where uom carries the quantity but defines this unit with a rounded literal, which is true of its imperial units. `psi` and `hp` are the two rows of the second kind, and `python/tests/test_units_cross_library.py` is what tells them apart from a unit uom defines exactly.

rust_ctor.description: The hand-written constructor in crates/azoth-core/src/units.rs that the generated conversion calls. The generator never invents one, and every unit of a dimension uom carries must name one - uom's own definition where it is exact, this crate's derivation where uom's literal is rounded - so the magnitude a unit converts to is a definition a reader can find. A constructor for a dimension uom carries returns the uom quantity; one for a dimension it does not returns the SI base magnitude directly.

id.description: The unit string a set names and a display shows, e.g. `degC`. Refused if it is also a `units` id, because a reader cannot tell which of the two a name meant.

pint.description: The unit's name in pint's registry. pint supplies the reference answer, which is what makes the two numbers below checkable.

factor.description: The unit's scale: one of it is this many SI base units, before the offset.

offset.description: The affine constant, in **the same unit as `factor`'s SI base** - uom's own convention, `si = (value + offset) * factor`, which is what makes °C `(u + 273.15) * 1` and °F `(u + 459.67) * 5/9`. A display inverts it, `u = si / factor - offset`, and a scale unit is the same expression with an offset of zero.

id.description: The set's id, which is what a caller switches to: `si`, `field`.

name.description: The set's name as a reader sees it.

units.description: One dimension per key, and the unit it is read in as the value. The generator refuses a key that is not a declared dimension, a value that is not a declared unit, and a value whose own dimension is not the key - a set that switched a quantity to a unit of another quantity would convert nothing - and it refuses two sets that name different dimensions, so switching to one and back is the same document.
